statement: The 1825-1831 "Black War" is documented as the most intense frontier conflict in Australian history (Nicholas Clements, The Black War: Fear, Sex and Resistance in Tasmania, University of Queensland Press, 2014: close to 200 British colonists and roughly 1,000 Aboriginal Tasmanians died violently in this period). George Augustus Robinson's "Friendly Mission" (1830-1834) relocated surviving Palawa groups, working through Aboriginal intermediaries Truganini, Woorrady, and Mannalargenna, under a promise of eventual return to Country that was never honored; internment at Wybalenna, Flinders Island, began 1833 (approximately 180 people relocated, ~130 died there, ~25 more died in transit), closed 1847 with fewer than 50 survivors moved to Oyster Cove. Pre-contact Tasmanian Aboriginal population estimates and precise death tolls are genuinely scholarly-disputed, not settled: Lyndall Ryan (Tasmanian Aborigines: A History Since 1803, Allen & Unwin, 2012) proposes ~7,000 pre-contact; Keith Windschuttle (The Fabrication of Aboriginal History, Vol. 1, Macleay Press, 2002) explicitly disputed Ryan's and Henry Reynolds's death-toll figures and their use of "genocide," prompting a collected scholarly rebuttal volume (Reynolds, Cassandra Pybus, Ryan, Martin Krygier, Neville Green); Reynolds has himself conceded the exact Aboriginal death toll "is likely to remain unknown."
scholarly_disagreement: Precise pre-contact population and death-toll figures for the Black War period are disputed between Windschuttle's skeptical revisionism and the Ryan/Reynolds/Clements mainstream; the broad fact of catastrophic, near-total population collapse by the 1830s is not seriously contested by either side.

interpretations.position: Pre-contact population was substantially higher (~7,000+) and death tolls from violence were severe, amounting to a documented catastrophic collapse verging on genocide
interpretations.strongest_case: Multiple independent quantitative reconstructions converge near Ryan's estimate at the upper end of carrying-capacity models.

interpretations.position: Ryan and Reynolds exaggerated death-toll figures and misapplied "genocide" to the historical record
